scope: Actual unchanged published macOS universal Unity players v0.1.0 and v0.3.0 executed on arm64; archive digests match GitHub release metadata.
Only ordinary JSON experiment/system configuration edited in fresh disposable extractions; compiled executable/managed-library/engine bytes hashed unchanged before and after each run.

Both single JSON and multipart topic/JSON tested against both players; actual sensor and world-transform recordings checked, including heading wrap, TCP publisher close/rebind and five repeated full scene reloads.
The fixture is explicitly synthetic, not camera tracking. Sample-video engine/recording coverage is tested separately.

Functional motion/transport compatibility passes all four cases. Unchanged v0.1.0 still logs existing receiver-thread join timeouts; it does not meet the strict clean-lifecycle gate. v0.3.0 passes both gates.
v0.1.0 also reports its old MasterDataLogger sharing violation during quit. Raw per-rig recordings were retained independently of that archive error.
No native Windows/Linux Unity-player, physical display or animal tracking claim.

legacy_v010_lifecycle_source.reason: The main thread disposes a subscriber whose worker can be blocked in ReceiveFrameString, waits only 500 ms, then discards the thread reference. Publisher protocol cannot change receiver ownership/lifetime.
